newsitem.title: UK: British poll shows little support for Goldsmith.
newsitem.headline: British poll shows little support for Goldsmith.

text.p: Billionaire Sir James Goldsmith suffered a setback when a leaked opinion poll showed his Referendum Party had virtually no support from British voters, newspapers said on Thursday.

A survey carried out privately for the party, which is campaigning for a referendum on Britain's relations with the European Union, showed that fewer than 0.5 percent of voters planned to back Goldsmith at the next general election, due by May.

The newspapers said top party officials were so dismayed that they requested the MORI polling organisation to ask different questions to get better results. But MORI refused and has now pulled out of its contract with the Referendum Party.
Goldsmith has spent an estimated 20 million pounds ($33 million) on his campaign and the ruling Conservative Party had feared he would split its vote, but that now seems unlikely.
The party plans to contest all the seats at the election except those where candidates of one of the main parties has come out in support of a referendum on the European Union.
